name: Virtual Asset Laundering via Mixers, Tumblers and Chain-Hopping
description: Criminals obscure the trail of virtual asset proceeds by routing them through mixing services, privacy-enhancing tools and rapid conversions between assets and blockchains. The aim is to break the link between illicit source and final cash-out point. Regulated platforms see this as exposure to mixers, layered swaps and unusually fast pass-through.

sources.text: FATF, Virtual Assets: Red Flag Indicators of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (2020)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)
FinCEN, Advisory on Illicit Activity Involving Convertible Virtual Currency (FIN-2019-A003, 2019)

FinCEN, Proposal of Special Measure Regarding Convertible Virtual Currency Mixing as a Class of Transactions of Primary Money Laundering Concern, Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, 88 FR 72701 (23 Oct 2023)

indicators.name: Deposits with direct or indirect exposure to mixing services
indicators.canon: Deposits with direct or indirect exposure to mixing services
indicators.desc: Incoming virtual asset transfers trace to known mixer or tumbler clusters within a small number of hops.
indicators.ctx: Incoming virtual asset transfers trace to known mixer or tumbler clusters within a small number of hops.
indicators.fp: Users of privacy tools for lawful privacy reasons, or exposure via a long, diluted transaction chain.

indicators.name: Rapid sequential conversions across many asset types
indicators.canon: Rapid sequential conversions across many asset types
indicators.desc: Funds received are swapped through several tokens or stablecoins in quick succession with no apparent trading rationale before withdrawal.
indicators.ctx: Funds received are swapped through several tokens or stablecoins in quick succession with no apparent trading rationale before withdrawal.
indicators.fp: Active traders, arbitrageurs and market makers.

indicators.name: Chain-hopping through bridges shortly after deposit
indicators.canon: Chain-hopping through bridges shortly after receipt
indicators.desc: Virtual assets are moved across chains or bridges and converted soon after being received.
indicators.ctx: Assets are deposited, then moved across blockchains via bridges or wrapped tokens within minutes or hours.
indicators.fp: Legitimate multi-chain users and liquidity providers.

indicators.name: Preference for privacy-enhanced coins with no commercial rationale
indicators.canon: Use of mixers, privacy coins or privacy pools around platform activity
indicators.desc: Funds pass through mixers, privacy coins or privacy-preserving pools before or after platform activity without commercial rationale.
indicators.ctx: Customer converts mainstream assets into anonymity-enhanced coins and withdraws them, or requests such assets despite a simple stated purpose.
indicators.fp: Privacy-conscious users; genuine holdings of such assets.

indicators.name: Withdrawals to many fresh addresses in fixed amounts
indicators.canon: Transfers to many newly created crypto addresses
indicators.desc: Repeated small or fixed-amount transfers to many fresh or new crypto addresses.
indicators.ctx: Balances are split into many near-identical outputs sent to newly created wallets (peeling or splitting pattern).

indicators.name: Use of anonymising network access to the platform
indicators.canon: Use of anonymising network access to the platform
indicators.desc: Sessions originate from Tor, rotating proxies or VPNs inconsistent with declared residence, combined with high-value transfers.
indicators.ctx: Sessions originate from Tor, rotating proxies or VPNs inconsistent with declared residence, combined with high-value transfers.
indicators.fp: Widespread lawful VPN use for privacy or security.

indicators.name: Very short holding time between receipt and exit
indicators.desc: Funds received into an account are forwarded onward within a very short period, often in near-equal amounts and leaving minimal balance.
indicators.ctx: Account behaves as a pass-through: most inbound value leaves within hours with minimal balance retained.

indicators.name: Cash-out to high-risk or unregistered exchanges
indicators.canon: Funds sent to unlicensed or weakly regulated exchanges
indicators.desc: Withdrawals or flows go to exchanges or VASPs that lack licensing or effective AML and sanctions controls.
indicators.ctx: Withdrawals go to addresses attributed to exchanges that lack licensing or effective AML controls.
indicators.fp: Attribution errors; unlicensed status may be unknown to user.

indicators.name: Customer unable to explain transaction purpose or origin
indicators.canon: Unable or unwilling to explain transaction purpose or origin
indicators.desc: When asked about a transaction, the customer gives vague, rehearsed, inconsistent or shifting explanations of its purpose, source or counterparties.
indicators.ctx: Explanations for layered transfers are vague, inconsistent or shift when challenged.
indicators.fp: Inexperienced users who do not understand the tooling.

indicators.name: Interaction with addresses linked to sanctioned or designated mixers
indicators.canon: Interaction with sanctioned or designated contracts, mixers or addresses
indicators.desc: Transfers touch contracts, pools, relayers or addresses designated by authorities or flagged in advisories.
indicators.ctx: Transfers touch addresses designated by sanctions authorities or flagged in official advisories.
